method: Rebuild from primary text. Cal. Lab. Code §2810.5 was fetched from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and read in full, in the version amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 451 (AB 636) effective January 1, 2024. The previous sources were three law-firm and trade-association blog posts; they have been replaced with the statute. CourtListener was searched for construing decisions and returned only a passing reference. Assertions describe the REBUILT body.
queries: "Labor Code" "2810.5" wage theft prevention notice hire

assertions.text: a written notice at the time of hiring, in the language the employer normally uses to communicate employment-related information
rate or rates of pay and the basis, including overtime rates as applicable
assertions.note: §2810.5(a)(1)(A). 'Including any rates for overtime, as applicable' was not in the previous body.

assertions.text: allowances claimed as part of the minimum wage, including meal or lodging allowances
the regular payday, the employer's name including any dba
the physical address of the main office or principal place of business, and a mailing address if different
assertions.note: §2810.5(a)(1)(E). The earlier check recorded this as NOT confirmed. It is confirmed, with the mailing address conditioned on being different — the previous body required both unconditionally.
§2810.5(a)(1)(F). Also recorded as NOT confirmed by the earlier check; confirmed.

assertions.text: the name, address and telephone number of the workers' compensation carrier
assertions.note: §2810.5(a)(1)(G). The previous body said only 'the workers' compensation carrier'.

assertions.text: a statement of paid sick leave rights: that the employee may accrue and use it, has a right to request and use it, may not be terminated or retaliated against for using or requesting it, and may complain about retaliation
assertions.note: §2810.5(a)(1)(H). Absent from the previous body and absent from its defect list — nobody had noticed it. It is a required element of the notice.

assertions.text: the existence of a federal or state emergency or disaster declaration applicable to the county or counties of employment, issued within 30 days before the employee's first day, that may affect their health and safety
assertions.note: §2810.5(a)(1)(I), added by AB 636. The clause's defect list had this without the 30-day window or the health-and-safety qualifier, both of which materially narrow it.

assertions.text: the Labor Commissioner publishes a template
assertions.note: §2810.5(a)(2). Since March 1, 2024 the H-2A template is posted on the Labor Commissioner's website.

assertions.text: a temporary services employer must additionally give the name, physical and mailing address and telephone number of the legal entity for whom the employee will perform work
assertions.note: §2810.5(a)(3), which excepts a licensed security services company providing only security services. Absent from the previous body.

assertions.text: written notice of any change within seven calendar days, unless every change is on a timely wage statement or in another writing required by law within seven days
assertions.note: §2810.5(b). Three corrections to the previous body: 'calendar' days; 'a timely wage statement' rather than 'the next wage statement'; and the second exception, which the previous body did not have.

assertions.text: 'employee' excludes state and local government employees, employees exempt from overtime by statute or wage order, and employees under a qualifying collective bargaining agreement
assertions.note: §2810.5(c)(1)-(3). The previous body addressed the notice to 'each non-exempt employee', which approximates (c)(2) and drops (c)(1) and (c)(3) entirely.

priorDefects: omitted: the paid sick leave statement in §2810.5(a)(1)(H) — a required element nobody had noticed.

omitted: the disaster declaration in §2810.5(a)(1)(I), which the defect list had recorded but the body did not carry, and which comes with a 30-day window and a health-and-safety qualifier the defect list did not have.
omitted: the address and telephone number of the workers' compensation carrier.
omitted: overtime rates as an element of the rate disclosure.
omitted: the temporary services employer additions in §2810.5(a)(3).
omitted: the public-employee and collective-bargaining exclusions in §2810.5(c)(1) and (3).
imprecise: 'the physical and mailing address of the main office' — the mailing address is required only if different.

imprecise: 'within seven (7) days of any change not shown on the next wage statement' — the section says seven calendar days, refers to a timely wage statement, and has a second exception for another writing required by law.
sources: three law-firm and trade-association blog posts, no primary text.
gaps: No decision construing §2810.5 was found on CourtListener; the only hit was a passing reference in Turrieta v. Lyft. The section appears unconstrued.

§2810.5(a)(4) and (d) require an employer of an H-2A agricultural worker to give a separate Spanish-language section covering a long list of additional rights, using the Labor Commissioner's template, from March 15, 2024. It was read and is not carried; an agricultural employer following this clause would be short of the section.

§2810.5(a)(1)(J) allows the Labor Commissioner to require any other information deemed material and necessary. What has been added is on the Labor Commissioner's template, which this session did not open. The clause notes the template exists and cannot say what is on it.
No penalty for failing to give the notice appears in §2810.5 itself and none was researched. The clause states a duty with no consequence attached.

sources.title: California Legislative Counsel (leginfo) — Cal. Lab. Code §2810.5 (as amended by Stats. 2023, Ch. 451 (AB 636), eff. Jan. 1, 2024)

noCaseLawNote: CourtListener returned one result for §2810.5, Turrieta v. Lyft, and it is a passing reference rather than a construction. The check was made.
singleHostNote: This finding rests on one host, leginfo.legislature.ca.gov. It is the publisher of the California codes, but it is one host, and the corpus's standard treats corroboration as requiring two. Nothing here meets it.
